reason: The text explicitly describes a well-organized hierarchical structure essential to the rebuilding effort. Leadership roles are clearly delineated: Yeshua ben Yotzadak (high priest) and the priests occupy one tier; Zerubbabel ben Shealtiel (civic leader) occupies another; the Levites are appointed from age twenty onward to specific oversight roles ('letzitze'ach al-melechet bet-YHVH' - to oversee the work of the Lord's house). Priests are assigned to play trumpets, Levites (sons of Asaph) to cymbals, and the text explicitly references the hierarchical authority established by King David. The organization is not discouraging hierarchy but rather implementing it as fundamental to proper worship and construction.
